note: An empty interface is a valid top-level declaration.
Interface requirements may declare parameters, return values, error sets, and generic parameters without receivers or bodies.
A read-only concrete receiver method satisfies a receiver-less interface requirement.
An editable concrete receiver method satisfies a receiver-less interface requirement.
A conforming type supplies every method required by one interface.
A record may explicitly implement multiple interfaces.
Generic interface requirements match alpha-equivalent generic concrete methods.
Fallible success and error channels are part of an interface method contract.

contains: interface method requirements cannot declare a receiver
note: The receiver is specified only by implementations and is forbidden in interface declarations.

contains: interface method requirements cannot have a body
note: Interface method requirements end in semicolons and cannot provide bodies.
An interface cannot require the same method name twice while receiver-method overloading is unsupported.

contains: interface `Readable` is declared more than once
note: Two top-level interfaces cannot share one name.
A declared implementation must supply every required receiver method.
Concrete method parameter types must exactly match the interface requirement.
Concrete method parameter arity must exactly match the interface requirement.
Concrete method success types must exactly match the interface requirement.
Concrete method error sets must exactly match the interface requirement.
Every name in an implements list must resolve.
A record type cannot appear in an implements list.
One type cannot list the same interface twice.
A same-named free function does not satisfy a receiver-method requirement.
Incompatible same-name requirements cannot be implemented until receiver-method overloading exists.
An inferred concrete type satisfying an interface bound is monomorphized and dispatched statically.
An explicit concrete type argument is checked against its interface bound.
A concrete generic argument that lacks declared conformance is rejected.
A generic parameter exposes no interface methods without a bound.
Receiver capability is checked when a specialization selects an editable witness for a read-only generic receiver.
An editable generic receiver may call a concrete witness with a read-only receiver.
A type parameter may require and use more than one interface bound.
Static interfaces cannot be used as runtime value types.
Two implementations produce concrete direct-call specializations and no vtable representation.
A heterogeneous variadic type pack lowers to concrete parameters and exposes an array-shaped compile-time length.
A variadic type pack may be empty.
Every element of a variadic type pack is checked against its interface constraint.
A single non-conforming element rejects the constrained variadic type pack.
Explicit type arguments following a variadic type parameter form its concrete type pack.

contains: variadic type parameter must be the final
note: A variadic type parameter must be last.

contains: variadic parameter must be the final
note: An array-shaped variadic value parameter must be last.

contains: generic parameter bounds or variadic shape differ
note: Generic interface method implementations must preserve the requirement's bounds under alpha-renaming.

contains: generic parameter bounds or variadic shape differ
note: A non-variadic generic method cannot satisfy a variadic interface requirement.
Interface constraints are validated even when the generic function is never instantiated.
Fixed constrained parameters and a final constrained type pack may coexist in one generic declaration.

contains: must be exported because it provides public conformance
note: A public type's conformance to a public interface cannot rely on a private witness method.

name: interface named import
note: An exported interface and its conformance survive a named module import.

name: interface namespace import and group export
note: A group-exported interface is usable as a namespace-qualified generic bound.

name: interface package metadata and consumer specialization
note: Generated package interfaces preserve exported interfaces, implements clauses, and concrete witness methods.
A generic function with a void success channel is specialized and emitted; both writers dispatch directly.
Interface bounds are enforced for a void-returning generic function, not just for one that returns a value.
Receiver capability is checked per specialization even when the generic function is declared after its caller.
An interface named as a record field type is reported as a constraint misuse, not as an undeclared name.

contains: is not supported on a type declaration's type parameter
note: Bounds are honoured only on functions, so a bound on a record type parameter is rejected instead of silently ignored.
An interface named as a by-value parameter type is reported once at the parameter, including when the function is called.
The generic-bound replacement for an interface-typed parameter specializes and mutates through the editable receiver.
